proposals.evidence: DEDR 5154 explicitly groups the exclusive first-person plural series, including Gondi mammoṭ, Kuwi māmbu, Gadaba/Parji ām, Tamil nāṅkaḷ, Telugu mēmu and Tulu eṅkuḷu. The source cognacy annotation independently identifies 5154. Tamil nānga and Tulu yankulu are retained as surveyed variants; source gloss we is unchanged. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 600 explicitly groups Gondi/Kota/Gadaba un-/uṇ- drink, Kurukh ōnnā and Malto óne/onde. The survey cognacy annotations point to this family; full article checking supports the same drinking verb. Kota unatukə and Malto hōnā remain intact as inflected/transcribed survey responses, with no silent truncation or normalization. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3559 gives the tōl/tokku skin/bark family with Gondi tōla bark, Kodagu tōlï skin, Gadaba tōl skin/bark, Tamil tōl skin and Toda twï·s̱ skin. Source cognacy explicitly identifies the article. Betta Kurumba tōlə is a comparative extension noted as a look-alike by the source; Gadaba tal and Toda tūrs preserve their survey vowel/consonant differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
